$ FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test  # chain-a
    The root-package check for the module-root corpus runs in normal runs, so it runs after the update: go test ./...
    what ran, in order:
        import ran
        parse ran on prices
        resolve ran on prices
        import ran
        parse ran on prices
        resolve ran on prices
--- PASS: TestCorpus
    --- PASS: TestCorpus/export
        --- PASS: TestCorpus/export/prices
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/export/prices/import
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/export/prices/parse
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/export/prices/resolve
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/export/prices/transform/louder
                --- PASS: TestCorpus/export/prices/transform/louder/import
                --- PASS: TestCorpus/export/prices/transform/louder/parse
                --- PASS: TestCorpus/export/prices/transform/louder/resolve
    --- PASS: TestCorpus/script
PASS

$ edit b/testdata/hypercase.json  # b's registry records another description for import
$ go test  # chain-a
    the registries that own or use the lift import differ in description:
          description:
            .: "Imports the export as a script, as its import/ tree says."
            ./b: "Imports the export."
        Every package that owns or uses a lift registers one declaration of it: a package that only uses a bytes lift tells by its own declaration whether an update writes the lift's cell, and so the cells past it. Declare the lift once, in a package the others import, and register that declaration. If they register one declaration already, a registry is stale: run FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./..., which rewrites the registry of every package with tests.
    what ran, in order:
        import ran
        parse ran on prices
        resolve ran on prices
        import ran
        parse ran on prices
        resolve ran on prices
--- FAIL: TestCorpus
    --- PASS: TestCorpus/export
        --- PASS: TestCorpus/export/prices
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/export/prices/import
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/export/prices/parse
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/export/prices/resolve
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/export/prices/transform/louder
                --- PASS: TestCorpus/export/prices/transform/louder/import
                --- PASS: TestCorpus/export/prices/transform/louder/parse
                --- PASS: TestCorpus/export/prices/transform/louder/resolve
    --- PASS: TestCorpus/script

$ edit b/testdata/hypercase.json  # b's registry records another description for parse
$ go test  # chain-a
    the registries that own or use the lift parse differ in description:
          description:
            .: "Parses the script, as its parse/ tree says."
            ./b: "Parses."
        Every package that owns or uses a lift registers one declaration of it: a package that only uses a lift runs its own declaration of it to stage the cells past it, and the lift's cell, which the package that owns it writes, records what the owner's declaration does. Declare the lift once, in a package the others import, and register that declaration. If they register one declaration already, a registry is stale: run FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./..., which rewrites the registry of every package with tests.
    what ran, in order:
        import ran
        parse ran on prices
        resolve ran on prices
        import ran
        parse ran on prices
        resolve ran on prices
--- FAIL: TestCorpus
    --- PASS: TestCorpus/export
        --- PASS: TestCorpus/export/prices
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/export/prices/import
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/export/prices/parse
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/export/prices/resolve
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/export/prices/transform/louder
                --- PASS: TestCorpus/export/prices/transform/louder/import
                --- PASS: TestCorpus/export/prices/transform/louder/parse
                --- PASS: TestCorpus/export/prices/transform/louder/resolve
    --- PASS: TestCorpus/script
